summary: Proposes a standard for gateway-to-gateway procedures that let gateways be mutually suspicious, as a draft inviting comments. This is the Exterior Gateway Protocol.

eli5.summary: Routers belonging to different groups need a way to share road maps without fully trusting each other. This memo proposes that way.

questions: how does egp neighbor acquisition work
subtitle: The first draft of how separately run gateway systems tell each other which networks they can reach.

tldr.problem: As the internet grew, having every gateway join one common routing algorithm became too costly and too rigid. Separately run systems of gateways needed a way to exchange reachability information without trusting each other.
tldr.mechanism: EGP has three parts: a neighbor acquisition handshake, a Hello and I Heard You exchange to track neighbor reachability, and polled Network Reachability messages that list the networks a gateway is an appropriate first hop for.
tldr.outcome: RFC 827 is a draft inviting comments, and it is updated by RFC 904. It says plainly that EGP is not a routing algorithm and assumes the autonomous systems form a tree with no cycles.

facts.label: Stub neighbors
facts.value: No more than two or three core gateways

today: RFC 827 describes itself as a draft inviting comments, and the unit metadata lists no formal status for it. It is updated by RFC 904, so check that document alongside this one.

sections.title: Why an Exterior Gateway Protocol
sections.content:
The Exterior Gateway Protocol (EGP) is offered as a draft standard for gateway to gateway procedures that let gateways be mutually suspicious. In the early internet, new gateways joined a single common routing algorithm. The RFC lists why that stops working as the network grows: the routing overhead becomes excessive, very different gateways make fault isolation nearly impossible, and the routing algorithm becomes too rigid because any change must be made in too many places.

The RFC expects the internet to become a set of autonomous systems, each a set of relatively homogeneous gateways that use a private routing algorithm. In the simplest case a system is a single stub gateway joining a local network to the rest of the internet. EGP lets one or more autonomous systems carry traffic between others, while the end user still sees a single internet with a flat address space.

Autonomous systems get 16-bit identification numbers, carried in every EGP message header, and zero means no number is present. Gateways that share a communications medium whose inner structure is transparent to them are neighbors: interior neighbors if in the same autonomous system, exterior neighbors if not. EGP is a polling protocol, so each gateway controls the rate at which it sends and receives reachability information.
sections.eli5: Each group of routers runs its own roads. EGP lets two groups swap just enough information to send cars across the border.

sections.title: Neighbor Acquisition
sections.content:
Before gateways can exchange routing information they must become direct neighbors, using a standard three-way handshake called the neighbor acquisition protocol. A gateway sends a Neighbor Acquisition Request, repeating it at a reasonable rate (the RFC suggests perhaps every 30 seconds or so) until it gets a Neighbor Acquisition Reply. The recipient may refuse, optionally giving a reason, or reply and also send its own request. Two gateways become direct neighbors when each has sent a request to, and received the matching reply from, the other.

A gateway that wants to stop being a neighbor sends a Neighbor Cease message, retransmits it up to some number of times, and the receiver must answer with a Cease Acknowledgment. The RFC does not specify how a gateway first decides that it wants to become a neighbor of another.
sections.eli5: Before two gatekeepers swap maps they shake hands both ways: I would like to be your neighbor, and so would I.

sections.title: Checking That Neighbors Are Alive
sections.content:
The neighbor reachability protocol uses two messages, Hello and I Heard You. A Hello from a direct neighbor must be answered with an I Heard You immediately, never more than a few seconds later. The RFC sketches a rule like declaring a neighbor unreachable if fewer than k answers arrive for the last n Hellos, but leaves the algorithm and its parameters to implementers, who may need to agree on them jointly.

Both messages carry a status field saying whether the sender thinks the receiver is reachable, which lets one gateway be passive and send only I Heard You messages, while the other actively sends Hellos. They also carry the ID of the last NR poll received and the minimum interval, in minutes, at which the sender is willing to be polled. A neighbor that becomes unreachable remains a neighbor, but if it stays unreachable for an extremely long time such as an hour, the gateway should stop treating it as one. A gateway that is going down should send a Gateway Going Down message so neighbors can prepare.
sections.eli5: Neighbors keep calling out Hello and the other answers I hear you. If the answers stop for long enough, you assume they are gone.

sections.title: Network Reachability Messages and Polling
sections.content:
A Network Reachability (NR) message lists the networks for which a gateway is an appropriate first hop, meaning there is no better gateway on that network to route toward them. Each network comes with a one-byte distance whose metric is left to each autonomous system. The value 255 means the network is unreachable and every other value means reachable. A network missing from one NR message is assumed still reachable, but if it is missing from two successive messages it is taken as no longer reachable.

The message can also name the sender's other interior and exterior neighbors on the same network, with the networks each is a first hop for. This lets a gateway discover neighbors and treat them as indirect neighbors: it forwards traffic to them directly without running acquisition, reachability or NR exchange with them. Large NR messages can be fragmented, and each fragment must be self-contained.

NR messages are sent in response to an NR Poll. No gateway may poll another more often than once per minute, and polls go only to neighbors declared reachable. A polled gateway must answer within several seconds. Between two polls it may send one unsolicited NR message, marked with the U bit. If no NR message arrives after the maximum number of poll retransmissions, the polling gateway assumes the other is not an appropriate first hop for any network.
sections.eli5: The map one gatekeeper hands over only lists the towns it is the best door to, and how far away each one is. If a town stops appearing on the map twice in a row, it is dropped.

sections.title: Stub Gateways and Limitations
sections.content:
The most common expected use is a stub gateway talking to one of the DARPA core gateways. The stub is configured with the addresses of no more than two or three core gateways and starts acquisition with them. Its NR message is as simple as possible: one data block headed by its own address, listing only the networks reachable no other way. The core gateways send complete NR messages, which lets the stub become an indirect neighbor of the other gateways. Core gateways report distances below 128 if a network can be reached without leaving the core system, and 128 or more otherwise. The stub must never forward traffic to a core gateway that is not an appropriate first hop, except for datagrams using the IP source route option.

The RFC is explicit about limits. EGP is not a routing algorithm, and it does not give enough information for a general area or hierarchical routing algorithm. If the topology of autonomous systems has cycles, it cannot prevent routing loops. If a gateway sends an NR message with false information, claiming to be a first hop to a network it cannot reach, traffic for that network may never be delivered.
sections.eli5: A small town with one gate only tells the big city about the places it alone can reach. The system works for simple branching layouts but not for tangled ones, and a gatekeeper who lies can send traffic nowhere.
